// NOTES: AWS AgentCore Gateway Deployment Configuration — Credential Vending + IS 7.3 OBO Integration
// DESCRIPTION: This config shows AgentCore's per-agent IAM roles, session tag mappings, and trust federation with IS 7.3 for RFC 8693 token exchange.
// PLACEHOLDERS: Replace all <PLACEHOLDER: ...> values with your AWS account IDs, ARNs, URLs, and credentials

agentcore_gateway.// service_role_arn: This role is assumed by AgentCore to vend credentials to agents

credential_vending.// credential_lifetime_seconds: 15 minutes — short-lived temporary credentials reduce leak blast radius

session_tags.// userId: Extracted from the user's IS 7.3 access token (sub claim); identifies which user initiated this agent session

session_tags.// agentId: Agent client ID from IS 7.3; identifies which agent instance made the call

session_tags.// sessionId: Generated by AgentCore; unique ID for this session; correlation ID between CloudTrail and IS 7.3 audit logs

credential_vending.// session_tag_usage: Session tags appear in CloudTrail as principal.sessionContext.sessionTags; enables fine-grained auditing and per-agent IAM policies

sigv4_signing.// algorithm: Signature Version 4 — signs every request with temporary IAM credentials; includes timestamp (prevents replay beyond credential TTL)

// SECTION 2: IAM ROLES PER AGENT TYPE.description: Each agent type (orchestrator, tool, mcp-client) gets a dedicated IAM role with scoped permissions

orchestrator.// trust_policy: Only AgentCore can assume this role; session name must start with 'orchestrator-' to prevent role confusion
orchestrator.// permission_policy: Orchestrator can read logs, get secrets, read config, and query session state — only when tagged as orchestrator

tool.// permission_policy: Tool role is narrower than orchestrator: can log, read user accounts (gated by agentId tag), and enqueue payments

// SECTION 3: TRUST FEDERATION WITH IS 7.description: AWS trusts IS 7.3 OIDC tokens as actor_tokens in RFC 8693 token exchange

external_oidc_providers.// oidc_discovery_url: IS 7.3 endpoint that publishes JWKS, token endpoint, and other OIDC metadata
external_oidc_providers.// trusted_audiences: The OIDC token's 'aud' claim must match one of these to prevent token reuse across different IS 7.3 instances or tenants

subject_mapping.// oidc_subject_claim: When AgentCore receives an OIDC token from IS 7.3, extract 'sub' (agent client_id)
subject_mapping.// mapped_to: Map the OIDC 'sub' to the session tag 'userId' in credential vending

// SECTION 4: TOKEN EXCHANGE ENDPOINT CO.description: IS 7.3 token exchange endpoint for RFC 8693 OBO flows

token_exchange.// is73_token_endpoint: AgentCore calls this endpoint when an agent needs a delegated token

exchange_flow.description: AgentCore agent → IS 7.3 OBO token exchange

step_1_agent_gets_user_token.description: User authenticates via App-Native Auth or OIDC; AgentCore receives user's IS 7.3 access token
step_1_agent_gets_user_token.// how: User session context is passed to AgentCore (e.g., via JWT, shared session store, or Bedrock context)

step_2_agent_assumes_role.description: AgentCore calls sts:AssumeRole with session tags (userId, agentId, sessionId)

step_3_agent_gets_oidc_token.description: AgentCore uses temporary credentials to fetch an OIDC identity token from AWS STS
step_3_agent_gets_oidc_token.token_format: JWT with claims: sub=agent_client_id, aud=is73_token_endpoint, iat, exp

step_4_agent_exchanges_for_is73_token.// parameters_explanation: subject_token = user's IS 7.3 token; actor_token = AgentCore's AWS OIDC token; client_assertion = agent's JWT for client auth

is73_validation: Verify actor_token signature against AWS OIDC JWKS
Verify actor_token aud claim matches IS 7.3 token endpoint
Verify subject_token is valid and not revoked
Apply actor trust policy: is this agent allowed to exchange for this user?
Narrow scope: requested scope must be subset of subject_token scope
Check may_act claim for pre-authorized agents

token_payload.// sub: Original user; preserved throughout the delegation chain
token_payload.// act: Acting principal (agent); nests on subsequent exchanges (tool agent exchange would add act.act)
token_payload.// exp: 15 minutes from now; short-lived agent tokens
token_payload.// jti: Unique JWT ID for tracing across IS 7.3 audit logs and API backend logs

// SECTION 5: DELEGATION CHAIN DEPTH LIM.description: Prevent infinite delegation chains; recommended max = 3 hops

delegation_constraints.// max_chain_depth: User → Orchestrator → Tool → Backend API = 3 hops

chain_structure.hop_1: User initiates; user token issued by IS 7.3
chain_structure.hop_2: Orchestrator exchanges user token; receives token with act.sub=orchestrator_id
chain_structure.hop_3: Tool exchanges orchestrator token; receives token with act.sub=tool_id, act.act.sub=orchestrator_id
chain_structure.// hop_3: Backend API receives token with full chain. API MUST validate act chain and verify each principal in the chain

depth_enforcement.mechanism: IS 7.3 actor trust policy per application
depth_enforcement.// mechanism: Console configuration specifies which exchanges are allowed at each hop

example_policy.// allowed_subject_types: Only user tokens can be exchanged; not other agent tokens (prevents 4+ hops)

// SECTION 6: AUDIT AND COMPLIANCE.description: Traceability across AgentCore CloudTrail, IS 7.3 audit logs, and backend API logs

correlation_ids.// session_id: Generated by AgentCore; propagated through all requests; links CloudTrail entries to IS 7.3 audit log to backend transaction log
correlation_ids.// jti: JWT ID in IS 7.3 token; links IS 7.3 token exchange event to backend API log

cloudtrail_entry.// notes: CloudTrail records every credential vending event; session tags are visible; connects to IS 7.3 via sessionId

is73_audit_log_entry.subject: <PLACEHOLDER: user_id>
is73_audit_log_entry.// notes: IS 7.3 audit log records token exchange with user identity, agent identity, and sessionId for correlation

backend_transaction_log_entry.// notes: Backend logs the full context; can correlate back to CloudTrail (via sessionId) and IS 7.3 audit (via jti)

revocation_propagation.trigger: User revokes session in mobile app
propagation_flow: 2. IS 7.3 marks user_token as revoked in database
3. Next introspection call returns active:false for user_token
4. IS 7.3 transitively marks all derived tokens as revoked (orchestrator_token, tool_token, etc.)
5. Backend API introspects agent token; receives active:false
6. Backend API denies request; logs: revocation_reason=parent_token_revoked, session_id=<PLACEHOLDER: session_id>
revocation_propagation.// notes: Revocation propagates within introspection cache TTL (5min for compliance); short agent token lifetimes (5min) minimize window of undetected revocation

high_availability: Deploy AgentCore in multiple AZs behind a load balancer
IS 7.3 in active-active cluster (3–5 nodes); database replicas for read-heavy introspection
Cache introspection results at API gateway level (APIM) with TTL matching token lifetime
CloudTrail enabled for all sts:AssumeRole calls; S3 bucket for long-term audit retention
monitoring: CloudWatch metrics: sts:AssumeRole call rate, error rate
IS 7.3 metrics: token exchange request rate, introspection request rate, cache hit ratio
Backend API metrics: revocation detection latency (time between user revocation and API denial)
Alerts: if introspection latency > 500ms or error rate > 1%
networking: AgentCore to IS 7.3: HTTPS with certificate pinning (prevent MITM)
AgentCore to AWS STS: VPC endpoint (keep traffic on AWS backbone)
Backend API to IS 7.3 introspection: VPC endpoint (reduce cross-region latency)
